high.label: 690 V three-phase, 60 Hz
high.text: Where her power is made: the three generators and the main switchboard, and the largest motors on it (the bow thruster). Three-wire, insulated from the hull, earth-fault lamps on the board.

main.label: 440 V three-phase, 60 Hz
main.text: The rest of her power, through two 690/440 V transformers, either of which carries it: pumps, fans, the steering gear, the ramps, the galley range and the water heater. Three-wire, insulated. The shore connection and the emergency generator are 440 V.

small.label: 230 V, 60 Hz
small.text: Lighting, small power and the bridge, through 440/230 V transformers: two-wire, both poles insulated and both switched.

dc.label: 24 V direct current
dc.text: Two-wire, insulated, from two battery banks in the emergency generator room. The general service bank feeds navigation and control and is the transitional source: it carries the general alarm, the public address, the transitional lighting and, through an inverter, the navigation lights through the 45 seconds the emergency generator takes to start, and for half an hour if it does not. The radio bank feeds the radio and nothing else. Each bank floats on its own charger.

sources.name: 24 V battery bank, general service and transitional

elsewhere.name: Main switchboard, 690 V
elsewhere.text: The three generators in parallel, the bow thruster, and the two transformers to the 440 V section.

elsewhere.name: Main switchboard, 440 V section
elsewhere.text: Behind two 690/440 V transformers, either of which carries it; the shore connection comes in here. Her motors other than the thruster.

elsewhere.name: Lighting and small-power board
elsewhere.text: The 230 V section of the main board, behind the 440/230 V lighting transformers.

elsewhere.name: Emergency switchboard
elsewhere.text: A 440 V board, fed from the main board's 440 V section through the bus-tie while there is main power, and from the emergency generator within 45 s of losing it; its 230 V section, which feeds the bridge, is behind the 5 kVA emergency lighting transformer.

elsewhere.name: Emergency switchboard, transitional section
elsewhere.text: A section of the emergency switchboard that is never dead: fed from the board while it is alive, and without a break from the general service battery through a 1 kVA inverter (24 V DC to 230 V) when it is not. It feeds the navigation light panel.

elsewhere.name: 24 V DC board, general service bank
24 V DC board, radio bank
elsewhere.text: The reserve source of energy of the radio installation: it feeds the radio and nothing else.

elsewhere.name: Steering gear power unit No. 1, control circuit
Steering gear power unit No. 2, control circuit

rules.text: A breaker is at least 1.25 times the full-load current; a cable is rated for its breaker; no cable loses more than 5 % of the voltage, and no consumer more than 6 % in all from the switchboard (10 % on a battery supply). A cable's length is the way it is laid along, and a tenth more.

subsystems.name: Navigation
subsystems.text: Finding where she is, where she heads and what is around her: radar, charts, position, heading, depth, speed, wind.

subsystems.name: Steering
subsystems.text: From the wheel, the tiller or the autopilot to the two rudders, and the rudder angle shown back.

subsystems.name: Propulsion control
subsystems.text: The two main engines, their gearboxes and the bow thruster, worked from the bridge and from either wing.

subsystems.name: Radio
subsystems.text: Distress and safety radio for sea area A1 (within VHF range of the coast), and the float-free and portable sets.

subsystems.name: Internal communication
subsystems.text: Public address and general alarm, talkback to the mooring stations and the ramp, the telephones.

subsystems.name: Alarm and monitoring
subsystems.text: What the bridge is told without asking: machinery alarms, the watch alarm, doors and ramp, the cameras.

subsystems.name: Fire detection and fire-fighting
subsystems.text: The detection loop and its panel, call points, extinguishers, the hydrant and hose.

subsystems.name: Navigation lights and signals
subsystems.text: The lanterns and their monitored panel, the whistle, the searchlight, wipers, flags and the signalling lamp.

subsystems.name: Lighting
subsystems.text: White light for work, red for the night watch, emergency lighting, the wings and the foredeck.

subsystems.name: Electrical distribution
subsystems.text: The boards on the bridge and the cable ways from them.

subsystems.name: Air conditioning
subsystems.text: The wheelhouse room unit and its condensing unit on the compass deck.

subsystems.name: Piping
subsystems.text: Compressed air to the whistle, fresh water to the window wash, the fire main, the scuppers.

subsystems.name: Life-saving
subsystems.text: Lifebuoys, lifejackets for the watch, pyrotechnics, first aid.

subsystems.name: Emergency power
subsystems.text: The emergency generator set in its own room, with what starts it, feeds it, cools it and takes its exhaust away, and the emergency switchboard it supplies.

subsystems.name: Stern ramp and door
subsystems.text: The leaf, its hinges and cylinders, its end flaps, the ten cleats that hold it shut, their switches, and the stand it is worked from.

subsystems.name: Cargo access hydraulics
subsystems.text: The power pack in the hydraulic pump room, its pumps, valves, filters and cooler, and the pipes to the stern.

subsystems.name: Power generation
subsystems.text: The three diesel generating sets in the auxiliary engine room. Not installed: their places are marked.

subsystems.name: Outfit
subsystems.text: The room itself and its furniture: console, stand, chairs, chart table, doors, windows, linings.

boards.name: Wheelhouse distribution board
boards.text: General services of the bridge: lighting, wipers, sockets, the air conditioner, the chart system, the pantry. Dead in a blackout.

boards.name: Wheelhouse emergency distribution board
boards.text: What must work when the main board is dead: the radar, public address and general alarm, the emergency light, the whistle, the second supply of the propulsion control. Fed from the emergency switchboard, so from the main generators while they run and from the emergency generator when they do not. The navigation lights and the fire detection panel are not on it: each has feeders of its own, direct from the switchboards.

boards.name: 24 V DC panel, navigation and control
boards.text: Navigation sensors, steering and propulsion control, alarms, the red night lighting: on the general service battery, so nothing on it notices a blackout.

circuits.name: Navigation data: distributor, network switch, conning display
Alarm panel, watch alarm, door and ramp panel
Heading and bearing repeaters, rudder angle indicators
Public address and general alarm, battery supply
Night and transitional lighting, binnacle light

fedBy.name: 24 V DC board, general service bank

boards.name: 24 V DC panel, radio
boards.text: The radio installation on its own battery (the reserve source of energy): both VHF sets, the NAVTEX receiver, the position fix for the distress call, the portable sets' charger.

boards.name: Navigation light panel
boards.text: One fused and monitored way for each lantern: a lamp that fails sounds the buzzer and lights its lamp on the panel. Two feeders of its own, each direct from a switchboard and by a different way: the emergency switchboard's transitional section, which the battery keeps alive while the emergency generator starts, and the main lighting board as the second, with the change-over switch on the panel. The emergency feeder comes down the starboard duct, the main feeder round the port side and down the port duct: they meet in the console, at the panel.

boards.name: Stern ramp starter panel
boards.text: In the hydraulic pump room: an isolator, a star-delta starter for each main pump, direct starters for the cleats' pump and the cooler's fan, and the control transformer. Fed from the main switchboard's 440 V section, whose place is marked in the main switchboard room: its feeder is drawn the whole way there. Dead in a blackout: the ramp then stays where its load-holding valves hold it, and is worked by the hand pump.

circuits.name: Control transformer 440/24 V, 630 VA: stand, valves, switches

outside.name: Bridge deck lighting, corridor and after platform
Searchlight
outside.note: The Minato Maru's feeder, its own cable from the lighting board by the port casing trunk, with a 16 A breaker: that ship's list gives it 10 A for 9.5 A, which is under its own rule of 1.25 times the full-load current.

nets.name: Navigation data
nets.medium: IEC 61162-1 (NMEA 0183), 4800 baud, one twisted pair a line
nets.text: Every sensor talks to the distributor on its own line; the distributor gives each listener a buffered line of its own. A talker never has more than one listener to drive, and a short on one line stays on that line.

members.says: a buffered copy of every sentence, to each listener
GGA, RMC, VTG, ZDA: position, course and speed over the ground, time
HDT, ROT: true heading, rate of turn
VHW, VBW: speed through the water
position and time, for the distress call

nets.name: AIS targets
nets.text: The ships the AIS hears, to the radar and the chart system.

members.says: VDM, VDO: other ships and her own report

nets.text: The radar picture and the charts between the processor, the displays and the chart system.

nets.text: One cable from the processor to the turning unit on the mast.

nets.text: The cameras to the recorder and the monitor.

Camera at the stern
Camera in the engine room

Bow thruster starter and controller

Bow thruster starter and controller

nets.medium: 4 to 20 mA signal, screened pair, with its own supply
nets.text: The rudders' true angle from the transmitter on the steering gear to every indicator. It is independent of both control systems: it shows the truth when either has failed.

nets.medium: 100 V loudspeaker lines in zones; fire-resistant cable
nets.text: One amplifier, the microphone at the console, and loudspeakers in every space aboard. The general alarm goes out on the same lines.

members.ext: Loudspeakers on the car deck, in the saloon, the crew rooms, the machinery spaces and on the open decks

Station at the after mooring station

nets.text: The emergency line between the bridge, the engine control room and the steering-gear room.

Sound-powered telephone, for emergency steering

nets.text: The automatic telephone.

Sets in the cabins, the mess and the galley

nets.medium: a two-wire addressable loop, out and back, fire-resistant cable
nets.text: Bridge deck: every detector and call point on one loop that starts and ends at the panel, so a single break loses nothing.

members.ext: Detectors and call points in the corridor, the cabins, the mess, the galley and the two machinery rooms of the bridge deck
Loops 2 to 4 (passenger deck, car deck, machinery spaces), the alarm bells, the fan stops

nets.text: The alarm system in the engine control room to its panel on the bridge.

nets.text: The reset buttons to the watch alarm, and its calls out.

members.ext: Buzzers in the master's and the chief officer's cabins

nets.medium: 24 V, one pair to each limit switch
nets.text: Two switches on each closing (shut, and secured) to the lamps on the bridge.

members.ext: The five watertight doors below the car deck
The bow ramp and the three hatches in the car deck

nets.name: Whistle control
nets.text: The push buttons and the fog timer to the whistle valve.

nets.name: Wiper control
nets.text: The panel to the three wiper motors and the wash valve.

nets.name: Searchlight control
nets.text: The joystick to the searchlight's two motors and its lamp contactor.

nets.name: Instrument dimming
nets.text: One knob dims every instrument on the console together.

nets.text: To the transducer in her bottom.

nets.medium: 24 V, one pair to each solenoid, button and lamp
nets.text: From the starter panel's control circuit to the control stand and the valve stand: pump start and stop, raise and lower, the cleats' valve, the lamps.

members.says: starts the pumps, feeds the circuit

nets.name: Ramp and cleat position
nets.medium: 24 V, one pair to each switch
nets.text: Each of the ten cleats, both safety latches and both door posts has a switch. All home: "ramp closed and locked", green at the stand and on the bridge. Any away: red on the bridge.

members.ext: Ramp, hatch and watertight door panel (ALM-06)

nets.medium: 24 V, one pair to each switch

nets.name: Generators' feeders (placeholders)
nets.medium: 690 V three-phase, 2 x (3 x 120 mm2) a set
nets.text: From each generating set's place to the main switchboard's: 400 kVA at 690 V is 335 A a set. Not sized by this register; drawn so that the way is known.

nets.text: From the main switchboard to transformer No. 1 and on to the 440 V section.

pipes.name: Whistle air
pipes.text: From the working-air receiver in the engine room, up the pipe trunk, to the whistle valve over the helm and on up the mast to the two horns.

pipes.name: Window wash
pipes.medium: fresh water from the pressure set
pipes.text: A branch of the cold fresh-water main to the valve in the console, and from there through the port cant and round the bay outside, under its sill, to a nozzle at each wiper.

pipes.name: Fire main branch to the bridge deck
pipes.text: A branch of the fire main up the house side to the hydrant on the port wing.

pipes.name: Scupper, port wing
pipes.text: From the wing's deck down the house side and overboard above the waterline.

pipes.name: Scupper, starboard wing
pipes.text: From the wing's deck down the house side and overboard above the waterline.

pipes.name: Refrigerant lines
pipes.medium: refrigerant, a liquid line and a suction line, insulated
pipes.text: Between the room unit and the condensing unit above it.

pipes.name: Condensate drain
pipes.text: From the room unit through the house side to the starboard wing's deck, and so to its scupper.

pipes.name: Line A: the cylinders' rod sides
pipes.text: From the valve stand along the hydraulic room's wall and the port mooring station's, up, across over the door's head and to both cylinders. Oil here raises the ramp and holds it.

pipes.name: Line B: the cylinders' piston sides
pipes.text: Beside line A. Oil here lowers the ramp, against the load-holding valves.

pipes.name: Line C: cleats, lock
pipes.text: To a header down each mooring station's wall and across over the door's head: every cleat is fed from it by a hose.

pipes.name: Line D: cleats, let go
pipes.text: Beside line C. The two safety latches' lifting cylinders are on it too.

pipes.name: Pressure, pumps to valve stand
pipes.text: From the pressure block on the tank over the way to the valve stand.

pipes.name: Return, valve stand to tank
pipes.text: Back over the way, through the cooler and the return filter into the tank.

components.name: Console
components.what: The console block: 3.7 m wide on the centreline, standing free: a way 1.0 m wide runs before it in the forward bay, from one side way to the other, so that its back is reached for electrical work and maintenance. In its back each of its five bays has a service door on hinges with two quarter-turn locks; it opens to a tap on the bay's terminals: a rail of terminal blocks, the earth bar, the ship's cables up from a transit in the block's bottom, and the slotted duct by which the bay's units are wired. Over the doors a louvred vent for each bay. From aft: a stainless grab rail along its edge; a desk that slopes up 11° with two rows of flush panels on a dark field, and the three control heads in its after edge, at the hand; a level strip with the propulsion and thruster panels, each in line ahead of its levers; an upstand leaning back 20° with the displays set into it under glass, lower in the middle so that the sea is seen over it ahead of the wheel (nothing ahead of the wheel over 1.225 m, nothing else over 1.315 m: calculation JS4-402 asked 1.22 and 1.33). Below the desk a cabinet of five bays, each with two doors on hinges, a quarter-turn lock and louvres: they open to a tap, and the units that are not seen stand behind them on shelves.

components.name: Master's chair
components.what: A high-backed pilot chair in black leather at the conning position, to port of the wheel: headrest, armrests, a footrest, on a pedestal that runs on a track let into the deck and turns. A tap on its pedestal runs it aft or forward; a tap on its seat turns it.

components.name: Watch officer's chair
components.what: The second pilot chair, at the radar: like the master's, on its own track.

components.name: Chart table
components.what: The chart table against the aft wall, with three drawers for folded charts, which run out to a tap, and the chart in use on its top. She navigates on paper charts; the chart system on the console is an aid.

components.name: Bookshelf, nautical publications
components.what: Tide tables, the list of lights, the radio signals list, the signal code and the ship's own manuals, behind a fiddle rail.

components.name: Binoculars box
components.what: Two 7 × 50 binoculars in a varnished box on the console block's port end. Its lid lifts to a tap.

components.name: Stair well and rail
components.what: The head of the crew stair from the saloon, railed on its inboard side, with a self-closing gate across the top where one comes up: it opens forward, away from the well.

components.name: Watchkeeper's table
components.what: A table at the starboard side, forward of the pantry, 0.36 m broad so that the way past it to the front of the console block is 0.70 m: a top of light varnished wood with her profile engraved in it and a cup well in its corner, a drawer that runs out to a tap, the deck log under its own lamp. (It takes the place of the fold-down log desk that hung under the port window.)

components.name: Settee
components.what: A settee in black leather in the port wing, against its after wall beside the door from the open deck and under the after window, for the pilot and for whoever waits on the bridge. (It stood along the port side of the wheelhouse, where it closed the way past the console block to 0.46 m; the owner, 12 November 2026: "Move it to port wing". It is not in the wing's inboard corner: the fire hose box and the hydrant are there.)

components.name: Handrail under the sills, port
components.what: Stainless tube on brackets under the sills: from the middle of the bay round its port corner, along the cant and aft along the port side under the windows, in one length. Something to hold in a seaway while looking out. (It ended at the console block while the block stood against the front.)

components.name: Handrail under the sills, starboard
components.what: Stainless tube on brackets under the sills: from the middle of the bay round its starboard corner, along the cant and aft along the starboard side over the watchkeeper's table. It meets the port rail in a sleeve on the centreline.

components.name: Hook rail
components.what: A board of light wood with four brass hooks under the after port window, for oilskins and the watch's lifejackets.

components.name: Door, corridor to wheelhouse
components.what: The door from the crew corridor. It opens into the wheelhouse and is kept shut at night to keep the corridor's light off the glass.

components.name: Deck covering
components.what: Blue sheet vinyl on the steel deck, turned up every wall as a coved skirting; ribbed rubber mats at the helm and before the console; the two tracks the pilot chairs run on are let into it.

components.name: Deckhead lining
components.what: Strips of off-white panel running athwartships under the compass deck, a shadow gap between each two; the cable trays lie above them.

components.name: Overhead grab rail, port
components.what: A rail under the deckhead to hold on to in a seaway.

components.name: Overhead grab rail, starboard
components.what: A rail under the deckhead to hold on to in a seaway.

components.name: Overhead console
components.what: Two sloped consoles under the deckhead over the block, either side of the instruments that hang between them: the camera monitor to port, the two VHF sets to starboard. They hang above the windows' head, so that they hide nothing the glass would show.

components.name: Sun blinds
components.what: A roller blind of tinted film in a cassette at the head of each of the bay's five windows, on two guide wires. A tap draws one down, and lets it up again.

components.name: Door to the port wing
components.what: A weathertight door, hinged on its forward edge, with a glazed upper half and a 0.15 m sill. It stands opposite the starboard one: the Minato Maru's stood in the aft corner, where the boards and their locker now have the wall to themselves.

components.name: Door to the starboard wing
components.what: A weathertight door, hinged on its forward edge, with a glazed upper half and a 0.15 m sill.

components.name: Wheelhouse plating, linings and windows
components.what: The house itself: plated outside, lined inside, a forward bay with canted corners, its five windows raked 10° under an eave, and windows down both sides: glass over 224° of the horizon from the helm.

components.name: Bridge wing, port: closed in
components.what: The wing was an open deck behind a bulwark 1.1 m high. It is closed in, as open wings are when a ship is refitted: the bulwark stays, glass stands on it between steel posts (five panes forward, leaning with the wheelhouse's own, three outboard), beside the house's forward corner a weathertight door opens outward onto the gallery before the bridge, a wall with a door closes its after end, and a roof is carried out from the wheelhouse's eave to her side. One band of windows runs across her whole breadth.

components.name: Bridge wing, starboard: closed in
components.what: Closed in like the port wing: glass on the bulwark between steel posts, a wall and a door aft, a roof from the wheelhouse's eave to her side.

components.name: Radar display
components.what: The radar picture, with target tracking: the display and its keyboard at the watch officer's chair, set in the console's upstand under a hood against the daylight.

components.name: Radar processor
components.what: The radar's processor unit: it takes the scanner's signal, the heading and the position, and gives the picture to the display and to the chart system.

components.name: Radar scanner
components.what: An X-band scanner on the mast platform: a turning unit and a 1.8 m array, 14.2 m above the waterline.

components.name: AIS transponder
components.what: Sends her name, position, course and speed on VHF and shows the ships that send theirs.

components.name: Electronic chart system
components.what: Her position on an electronic chart, with the radar's and the AIS's targets laid over it. An aid: the paper chart on the chart table is the chart she is navigated on.

components.name: GPS navigator
components.what: Position, course and speed over the ground from the satellites; it gives them to every set that needs them, the radios among them.

components.name: Echo sounder
components.what: The depth under the keel, drawn as a trace, with a shallow-water alarm.

components.name: Speed log
components.what: The speed through the water from a sensor in the bottom; shown on the conning display.

components.name: Navigation data distributor
components.what: Takes each sensor's sentences once and gives a buffered copy to every listener, so that no set can pull another's line down.

components.name: Conning display
components.what: Heading, rudder angle, both engines' revolutions, speed, depth and wind on one screen in front of the master's chair.

components.name: Satellite compass processor
components.what: Works out her true heading and rate of turn from the two antennas in the dome on the compass deck. It is the heading every set steers and plots by.

components.name: Autopilot control unit
components.what: Sets and holds a heading; it steers through the steering control unit like the wheel does.

components.name: Wind display
components.what: Wind direction and speed relative to the ship: a round instrument hung under the deckhead ahead of the helm.

components.name: Heading repeater, overhead
components.what: Her true heading on a compass card, hung under the deckhead ahead of the helm where the whole bridge reads it.

components.name: Bridge clock
components.what: A quartz clock on ship's time, hung under the deckhead. Its own battery.

components.name: Navigation network switch
components.what: The Ethernet switch of the navigation network.

components.name: Compass periscope
components.what: The magnetic compass on the compass deck, read from the helm through a tube and a mirror: it stands directly under the binnacle.

components.name: Bearing repeater, port wing
components.what: A heading repeater under an azimuth ring on a pelorus stand, to take bearings from the wing.

components.name: Bearing repeater, starboard wing
components.what: A heading repeater under an azimuth ring on a pelorus stand, to take bearings from the wing.

components.name: Ship's clock
components.what: A brass bulkhead clock over the chart table.

components.name: Barometer
components.what: An aneroid barometer.

components.name: Clinometer
components.what: Shows her list in degrees.

components.name: AIS antenna
components.what: The AIS's own VHF whip, 1.4 m.

components.name: GPS antenna
components.what: The GPS navigator's antenna dome.

components.name: Satellite compass antenna
components.what: Two satellite antennas in one dome, a known distance apart along her length: the heading is the direction from one to the other.

components.name: Magnetic compass and binnacle
components.what: The standard compass, on the centreline clear of steel and wiring, with a dimmed lamp. It needs no power to point.

components.name: AIS position antenna
components.what: A small satellite antenna for the AIS's own position fix.

components.name: Wind sensor
components.what: A cup anemometer and a vane at the starboard end of the flag yard.

components.name: Steering stand and wheel
components.what: The helm: an eight-spoke wheel on a stand. The wheel's shaft runs through a flanged bearing into the helm unit on the stand's top, where it turns two transmitters, one for each control system, and the pointer on the unit's lid that shows the rudder ordered. Where the wheel is put, the rudders follow: four degrees of wheel for one of rudder, and the spoke with the brass cap upright when they are amidships. On the page the wheel turns with the rudder.

components.name: Steering control system No. 1
components.what: The first of two control systems that have nothing in common. It compares the rudder ordered (by the wheel's first transmitter, or the autopilot) with the angle fed back from the gear and works the valves of power unit No. 1. Its supply comes from that power unit's own circuit in the steering-gear room, and its cables go down the port side.
components.hid: inside the steering stand, port half

components.name: Steering control system No. 2
components.what: The second control system: the wheel's second transmitter, its own amplifier, the valves of power unit No. 2, a supply from that unit's circuit (which comes by the emergency switchboard), and cables down the starboard side. Either system steers her alone; the selector on the stand chooses.
components.hid: inside the steering stand, starboard half

components.name: Steering mode selector and tiller
components.what: Chooses the control system (No. 1 or No. 2) and hand steering, autopilot or the tiller. The tiller works the valves of the chosen power unit directly (non-follow-up): the rudders move while it is held over, and it needs neither amplifier. It stands in a gate, a slot across the ship; a tap holds it over or lets it go.

components.name: Heading repeater
components.what: The heading in figures, low on the stand's face: read by looking down, not through it.

components.name: Rudder angle indicator, overhead
components.what: The rudders' true angle, from the transmitter on the steering gear: a round instrument hung under the deckhead, read from anywhere in the wheelhouse.

components.name: Rudder angle indicator, console
components.what: A second indicator among the propulsion instruments. It sits on the console, not on a stand-off, so that the sea is seen over it (calculation JS4-402).

components.name: Engine control lever, port
components.what: One lever for the port engine: ahead or astern through the gearbox, then revolutions. It stands in the desk's after edge, at the hand, and its panel and the engine instruments are read over it. A control head: the lever turns on a shaft inside the housing and comes up through a slot in its top plate; a drum on the shaft closes the slot under it, and where the arm crosses the plate is its reading on the scale beside it, from full astern through stop to full ahead. Pushed forward is ahead. A tap moves it a notch, and the port engine's lever on each wing moves with it.

components.name: Engine control lever, starboard
components.what: One lever for the starboard engine, a control head like the port one's. A tap moves it a notch, and its fellow on each wing moves with it.

components.name: Bow thruster lever
components.what: Thrust to port or starboard from the tunnel thruster in the bow. A control head whose slot lies across the ship: the lever is pushed the way her bow is to go. A tap moves it a notch, with its fellow on each wing.

components.name: Propulsion control panel
components.what: Which station has control (bridge, a wing, or the engine control room), engine start and stop, and an emergency stop for each engine under a flap. On the level strip, in line ahead of the two engine levers and under their instruments.

components.name: Bow thruster panel
components.what: Start, stop, running lamp and the motor's current. On the level strip, in line ahead of the thruster lever.

components.name: Engine instrument panel
components.what: Revolutions of both engines, their oil pressure and cooling-water temperature. Low on the console, straight ahead of the wheel: the sea is seen over it (calculation JS4-402).

components.name: Propulsion control unit, bridge
components.what: Reads the levers at the three stations, decides which one commands, and sends the orders to the engine room over two CAN lines.
components.note: Two supplies from different sources: the general service battery, and the emergency board through a rectifier of its own in the same case; the loss of either gives an alarm. If both control lines are lost the engines hold the speed and direction last ordered, the alarm sounds on the bridge and in the engine control room, and control is taken at the engines.

components.name: Wing control station, port
components.what: Engine and thruster levers at the hand, and over them, in an upright face that leans back to the eye, a rudder angle indicator and a revolution indicator, each in line ahead of the lever it answers and read over it; at the outboard forward corner of the wing, for berthing port side to. The levers are outboard: standing at them she is seen along her side, and across the bow past the house to 45° on the other side.

components.name: Wing control station, starboard
components.what: Engine and thruster levers at the hand, and over them, in an upright face, a rudder angle indicator and a revolution indicator read over the levers; at the outboard forward corner of the wing, for berthing starboard side to. The levers are outboard, as on the port wing.

components.name: VHF radiotelephone No. 1, with DSC
components.what: The distress and calling set: 25 W, digital selective calling on channel 70 with her position from the GPS. In the starboard overhead console, with its handset in a cradle beside it on a coiled cord: the handset lifts to a tap.

components.name: VHF radiotelephone No. 2
components.what: The second set, for port and working channels, and the spare for the first: in the starboard overhead console.

components.name: NAVTEX receiver
components.what: Prints navigational and weather warnings broadcast on 518 kHz: on a bracket on the after wall over the chart table, where the warnings are plotted.

components.name: Portable VHF sets and charger
components.what: Three waterproof two-way sets for the survival craft, kept charged in their rack.

components.name: Radar transponder, port
components.what: A search and rescue transponder beside the port door, to be taken into a survival craft: it answers a searching radar. Its own battery.

components.name: Radar transponder, starboard
components.what: The second transponder, beside the starboard door. Its own battery.

components.name: Float-free EPIRB
components.what: A satellite distress beacon in a bracket that lets it go and float free if she sinks. Its own battery.

components.name: VHF antenna No. 1
components.what: A 3 m whip on the starboard side.

components.name: VHF antenna No. 2
components.what: A 3 m whip on the port side.

components.name: NAVTEX antenna
components.what: A short active antenna for 518 kHz.

components.name: Public address and general alarm amplifier
components.what: A 240 W amplifier with the general alarm's tone generator: seven short blasts and a long one on every loudspeaker aboard.
components.note: Two supplies: the emergency board, and the general service battery as the transitional source, taken over without a break when the board is dead.

components.name: Public address and talkback panel
components.what: The microphone, the zone keys (car deck, saloon, crew, open decks), the general alarm key, and the talkback keys for the two wings, the mooring stations, the ramp and the engine control room.

components.name: Telephone
components.what: The ship's automatic telephone: cabins, mess, galley, engine control room. Its handset lies in a cradle beside it on a coiled cord, and lifts to a tap.

components.name: Sound-powered telephone
components.what: Speaks to the engine control room and the steering-gear room with no supply at all: the voice makes the current, and a hand crank rings the other end. A cased wall set on the console block's starboard end; its handset lifts to a tap.

components.name: General alarm push button
components.what: Sounds the general alarm from the door.

components.name: Loudspeaker, wheelhouse
components.what: A loudspeaker in the deckhead.

components.name: Talkback station, port wing
components.what: A weatherproof loudspeaking station on the house side, under the forward window's sill (the window was carried forward where it hung, and the door to the gallery stands at the corner).

components.name: Talkback station, starboard wing
components.what: A weatherproof loudspeaking station on the house side.

components.name: Loudhailer
components.what: A horn loudspeaker on the mast platform, for hailing and for the fog signal's listening watch.

components.name: Machinery alarm panel
components.what: The engine room's alarms in groups, with a buzzer: the bridge sees that something is wrong below, and whether the engineer has accepted it.

components.name: Bridge watch alarm
components.what: Asks the watch to press a button every few minutes at night. Unanswered, it calls the master's cabin, then the general alarm.

components.name: Watch alarm reset, chart table
components.what: A reset button at the chart table.

components.name: Camera monitor
components.what: Four cameras on one screen: the bow ramp, the car deck, the stern and the engine room.

components.name: Ramp, hatch and watertight door panel
components.what: A lamp for the bow ramp, each hatch and each of the five watertight doors: green when shut and secured, red when not.

components.name: Camera recorder
components.what: Records the cameras.

components.name: Fire detection panel
components.what: The addressable fire detection panel: it names the detector that has answered, sounds the bells, and after two minutes unaccepted, the general alarm. It has a standby battery of its own.
components.note: Two feeders of its own, direct from the emergency and the main switchboard, with the automatic change-over switch in the panel and a fault alarm for each; and a battery of its own that carries it for half an hour, through the 45 seconds before the emergency generator is on the board.

components.name: Manual call point
components.what: Break the glass to give the alarm.

components.name: Smoke detector
components.what: An optical smoke detector on loop 1.

components.name: Sprinkler head, port
components.what: A pendent sprinkler head in the deckhead: its glass bulb bursts at 68 °C and lets the water out. The sprinkler main it stands on is not registered yet.

components.name: Sprinkler head, starboard
components.what: A pendent sprinkler head in the deckhead. The sprinkler main it stands on is not registered yet.

components.name: Fire extinguisher, CO₂ 5 kg
components.what: For the electrical equipment: carbon dioxide leaves nothing behind.

components.name: Fire extinguisher, powder 6 kg
components.what: Dry powder, beside the port door.

components.name: Fire hose box
components.what: A 15 m hose with a dual-purpose nozzle, coiled in its box beside the hydrant.

components.name: Navigation light panel
components.what: A switch, a fuse and a lamp-failure indicator for each lantern, on a mimic of the ship; a change-over switch between its two supplies. On the console block's apron, under the desk.

components.name: Sidelight, port
components.what: Red, from right ahead to 22.5° abaft the port beam: on the wing's roof at its outer end (it stood on the bulwark's rail while the wing was open), with a screen board inboard of it.

components.name: Sidelight, starboard
components.what: Green, from right ahead to 22.5° abaft the starboard beam: on the wing's roof at its outer end, with a screen board inboard of it.

components.name: Masthead light
components.what: White, over 225° ahead, on the front of the mast above the radar, its lens clear over the posts of the radar platform.

components.name: Anchor light
components.what: White, all round, on the crown of the mast.

components.name: Stern light
components.what: White, over 135° astern: on the centreline at the stern, on the bulwark's rail over the stern door, with a screen forward of it so that it is not seen from forward of the beam.

components.name: Not-under-command lights, upper pair
components.what: Red, all round: two heights of them in a vertical line, 2 m apart, say she cannot keep out of the way. Each height is a pair of lanterns, one either side of the mast, lit together: a single lantern beside the mast would be hidden by it over 35° of the horizon, and no more than 6° is allowed.

components.name: Not-under-command lights, lower pair
components.what: Red, all round: the lower pair, 2 m under the upper.

components.name: Whistle
components.what: Two air horns on the front of the mast, sounded by compressed air.

components.name: Whistle panel
components.what: A push button for the whistle and a timer for the fog signal (one long blast every two minutes when under way).

components.name: Searchlight control
components.what: A joystick that turns and tilts the searchlight, and its lamp switch.

components.name: Wiper and window wash panel
components.what: Each wiper on, off or intermittent, and the wash. A tap on a switch turns it a step, and its wiper runs.

components.name: Window wiper, starboard
components.what: A pendulum wiper on the outside of the starboard cant's glass, hung from its spindle in the window's head under the eave; its motor is inside, over the blind. A tap starts and stops it.

components.name: Window wiper, centre
components.what: A pendulum wiper on the outside of the glass ahead of the wheel, hung from its spindle in the window's head under the eave; its motor is inside, over the blind. A tap starts and stops it.

components.name: Window wiper, port
components.what: A pendulum wiper on the outside of the port cant's glass, hung from its spindle in the window's head under the eave; its motor is inside, over the blind. A tap starts and stops it.

components.name: Clear-view screen, port
components.what: A glass disc spinning in a ring in the window ahead of the master's chair: spray and rain are thrown off it, and it is clear where the window is tinted. Its motor is at its middle, carried by a tube from the rail under the window. A tap starts and stops it.

components.name: Clear-view screen, starboard
components.what: The second clear-view screen, in the window ahead of the watch officer's chair.

components.name: Window heating junction box
components.what: Where the forward windows' heated glass is fed and switched: a box let into the lining below the sill of the starboard cant, with its lamp.

components.name: Searchlight
components.what: A 1 kW searchlight on the compass deck, turned from the console.

components.name: Flag locker
components.what: The signal flags of the international code, each rolled in its own pigeonhole.

components.name: Daylight signalling lamp
components.what: A hand lamp for Morse by day, on its hook beside the starboard door with its socket.

components.name: Deckhead light
components.what: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

components.name: Deckhead light
components.what: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

components.name: Deckhead light
components.what: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

components.name: Deckhead light
components.what: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

components.name: Deckhead light
components.what: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

components.name: Deckhead light
components.what: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

components.name: Deckhead light
components.what: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

components.name: Deckhead light
components.what: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

components.name: Chart lamp
components.what: A dimmed lamp on a stalk, red or white, that lights the chart and nothing else.

components.name: Night light, red, port
components.what: A red light over the console: enough to find a switch by, without spoiling the night vision.

components.name: Night light, red, starboard
components.what: A red light over the console.

components.name: Emergency light
components.what: Lights by itself when the main supply fails.

components.name: Transitional light
components.what: A 24 V lamp on the general service battery: it lights at once when the supply fails, before the emergency generator has started.

components.name: Wing light, port
components.what: A bulkhead light on the house side, over the forward window (the window was carried forward under where it hung, and the door to the gallery stands at the corner: nothing is built over a window).

components.name: Wing light, starboard
components.what: A bulkhead light on the house side.

components.name: Dimmer panel
components.what: Dims the instruments, the red night lights over the console and the chart lamp. A tap on a knob turns it a step: the night lights and the chart lamp go out and come on with it, and the displays darken when the instruments are turned down.

components.name: Foredeck floodlight, port
components.what: Lights the car deck forward and the ramp.

components.name: Foredeck floodlight, starboard
components.what: Lights the car deck forward and the ramp.

components.name: Wheelhouse distribution board BD1
components.what: 230 V, from the lighting board in the engine control room: eight ways for the bridge's general services.

components.name: Emergency distribution board BD2
components.what: 230 V, from the emergency switchboard: six ways for what must not go dark.

components.name: 24 V DC panel DC1, navigation and control
components.what: 24 V from the general service battery: fifteen fused ways, a voltmeter and an earth-fault lamp.

components.name: 24 V DC panel DC2, radio
components.what: 24 V from the radio battery: five fused ways, a voltmeter and the charger-failure alarm.

components.name: Sockets below the sill, port
components.what: A double 230 V socket in the lining below the sill of the port cant.

components.name: Console socket
components.what: A 230 V socket on the console block's apron.

components.name: Console heaters
components.what: Small heaters low in the console that keep the damp out of the electronics when she lies cold.
components.hid: inside the console, at its foot

components.name: Pantry unit
components.what: A low unit under the starboard side window, wholly below its sill: the cooler in its after bay, the coffee maker in a niche with a rail across it for when she rolls, and under the niche a cupboard with the mugs, the coffee, the tea and the sugar. The cupboard opens to a tap.

components.name: Cooler
components.what: A 45-litre refrigerator for the watch: two wire shelves, a shelf in the door. It opens to a tap.

components.name: Coffee maker
components.what: A filter coffee maker with a glass jug on a hot plate: a litre and a quarter, a pot for the watch. A tap on its switch starts it, and the jug fills; a tap on the jug lifts and pours it, and it empties.

components.name: Pantry sockets
components.what: A double 230 V socket at the back of the pantry's niche, for the coffee maker and the cooler.

components.name: Cable transit at the mast
components.what: Where the cables to the mast and the compass deck pass the deck, sealed gastight and watertight.

components.name: Cable duct on the port mullion
components.what: A covered duct down a mullion of the bay and the lining under it, from the trays over the deckhead to a cable transit in the deck at its foot: the cables cross under the deck and come up into the console block, which stands free, through a transit in its bottom.

components.name: Cable duct on the starboard mullion
components.what: A covered duct down a mullion of the bay and the lining under it, from the trays over the deckhead to a cable transit in the deck at its foot: the cables cross under the deck and come up into the console block, which stands free, through a transit in its bottom.

components.name: Air conditioner, room unit
components.what: The wheelhouse's cooling and dehumidifying unit, high on the aft wall over the stair.

components.name: Air conditioner, condensing unit
components.what: The compressor and condenser, on the compass deck above the room unit.

components.name: Fire hydrant, port wing
components.what: A 50 mm hydrant on the fire main, with a hose coupling and a hand valve.

components.name: Scupper, port wing
components.what: The wing's deck drain, led overboard.

components.name: Scupper, starboard wing
components.what: The wing's deck drain, led overboard.

components.name: Whistle valve
components.what: The valve that lets air to the whistle: opened by a solenoid from the push buttons and the fog timer, or by hand with the pull above the helm.

components.name: Window wash valve
components.what: A solenoid valve on the fresh-water line to the wash nozzles.

components.name: Window wash nozzles
components.what: A brass pipe round the bay's head outside, under the eave, with a jet over each wiper's glass.

components.name: Lifebuoy with light and smoke, port
components.what: A lifebuoy on a quick-release with a self-igniting light and a smoke float: thrown from the wing for a man overboard.

components.name: Lifebuoy with light and smoke, starboard
components.what: A lifebuoy on a quick-release with a self-igniting light and a smoke float.

components.name: Locker: lifejackets and pyrotechnics
components.what: Four lifejackets for the watch, twelve parachute flares and the line-throwing appliance, under the boards.

components.name: First-aid kit
components.what: A first-aid box under the flag locker.

components.name: Emergency generator set No. 1
components.what: A six-cylinder turbocharged diesel and its alternator on one skid, on six rubber mounts: 440 V, three-phase, 60 Hz, 500 kW on the owner's drawing. Its radiator stands at its forward end in a cowl, so it needs no sea water. It starts by itself when the main board is dead.
components.note: 500 kW is the drawing's figure and is more than the 68 m ship's arrangement gives each of her main generators (about 320 kW); her own emergency loads come to something near 200 kW. The rating is one of the questions put to the owner with the general arrangement.

components.name: Starting battery bank, 24 V
components.what: Eight 12 V blocks in a steel rack, in two strings: they turn the starter, and nothing else is fed from them. The ship's transitional and radio batteries are not in this room.

components.name: Starting battery charger
components.what: Keeps the starting bank charged from the emergency switchboard; a voltmeter, an ammeter and a failure lamp.

components.name: Emergency generator control panel
components.what: Starts and stops the set, by itself or by hand; shows its voltage, frequency, load, oil pressure and temperature; the emergency stop is on its front. Fed from the starting battery.

components.name: Emergency switchboard, 440 V
components.what: Two sections: the generator breaker and the bus tie from the main board with their meters; and the ways to what must work when all else has stopped (steering, the emergency fire pump, emergency lighting, navigation lights, radio, alarms, the bilge pump).

components.name: Day tank, about 200 L
components.what: The set's own fuel, high enough to run to the engine by gravity: on a stand over a tray, with a level gauge, filled from the service tank.
components.note: 200 L is the drawing's figure. At full load 500 kW burns about 125 L an hour: the hours the rule asks of an emergency source are to be worked out with the rating.

components.name: Fuel quick-closing valve and its pull
components.what: Under the tank: shut by a wire from the red box outside the door, so that nobody goes into a fire to stop the fuel.

components.name: Exhaust: bellows, lagged riser, silencer
components.what: From the turbocharger through a bellows and a lagged riser up through the deckhead to a silencer on the roof.
components.note: The owner's drawing leads it to the funnel. Here it has a stack of its own, so the emergency set does not depend on the main machinery's casing.

components.name: Supply air duct and fire damper FD-01
components.what: Air for the engine and the room, in through a louvre on the forward wall; the damper shuts it. Its lever is worked by hand: tap it.

components.name: Exhaust air duct and fire damper FD-02
components.what: The room's warm air, out through a louvre on the starboard wall; the damper shuts it. Its lever is worked by hand: tap it.

components.name: Fuel lines
components.what: Supply from the day tank to the engine's filters and the return beside it, each tagged; the filling line from the service tank with its strainer and valve; the tank's vent, out through the wall.

components.name: Emergency generator room light No. 1
components.what: A fitting under the deckhead beams. Two of the four are on the emergency lighting: the one before the switchboard and the one over the way to the door.

components.name: Emergency generator room light No. 2
components.what: A fitting under the deckhead beams. Two of the four are on the emergency lighting: the one before the switchboard and the one over the way to the door.

components.name: Emergency generator room light No. 3
components.what: A fitting under the deckhead beams. Two of the four are on the emergency lighting: the one before the switchboard and the one over the way to the door.

components.name: Emergency generator room light No. 4
components.what: A fitting under the deckhead beams. Two of the four are on the emergency lighting: the one before the switchboard and the one over the way to the door.

components.name: Fire extinguisher, CO2 5 kg, emergency generator room
components.what: Carbon dioxide, for a fire in the switchboard or the set: by the door, under its sign.

components.name: Manual call point, emergency generator room
components.what: Break the glass to give the alarm: by the door one leaves by.

components.name: Heat detector, emergency generator room
components.what: A heat detector on loop 1 (a running diesel would set a smoke detector off).

components.name: Telephone, emergency generator room
components.what: To the wheelhouse and the engine control room.

components.name: Weathertight door, emergency generator room (house top)
components.what: A steel door with a porthole, two dogs and a lever handle, opening outward onto the deck: the escape route ends at it.

components.name: Stern ramp and door
components.what: One leaf, 11 m long and 9.4 m wide, a box girder 0.42 m deep, about 55 t. Raised, it is the stern door: it lies against a rubber seal round the opening; ten cleats hold it, and a safety latch on each door post that needs no oil. It turns on six hinges at the sill and lowers aft onto the quay: level at 90 degrees, and 4 degrees further for a quay that lies lower. Clear driveway 8 m, between the two cylinders.

components.name: Ramp hinges
components.what: Six along the sill: at each a lug of the ship stands out of the transom into a slot in the leaf's foot, and one pin of 90 mm goes through all of them. The hinge line lies 45 mm abaft the transom and 15 mm under the main deck, so that the roadway comes down level with the deck.

components.name: Ramp cylinder, port
components.what: Double-acting, bore 300 mm, rod 170 mm, stroke 3.40 m. Hung from a bracket under the upper deck's web beam at 3.6 m and pinned to a lug on the leaf 2.2 m from the hinge: 4.73 m between its pins with the ramp raised, 7.87 m with it level. It pulls: at most 952 kN, 198 bar on its rod side. A load-holding valve is bolted to it: if a hose bursts the ramp stays where it is.

components.name: Ramp cylinder, starboard
components.what: Double-acting, bore 300 mm, rod 170 mm, stroke 3.40 m. Hung from a bracket under the upper deck's web beam at 3.6 m and pinned to a lug on the leaf 2.2 m from the hinge: 4.73 m between its pins with the ramp raised, 7.87 m with it level. It pulls: at most 952 kN, 198 bar on its rod side. A load-holding valve is bolted to it: if a hose bursts the ramp stays where it is.

components.name: End flaps
components.what: 8 flaps of 1.1 by 1.2 m across the ramp's end, each on its own hinge: they lie on the quay and take up her list. Stowed, they lie folded back over the roadway; they fold out as the ramp comes down.

components.name: Door seal
components.what: A rubber strip on the transom round the opening's sides and head: the raised ramp is drawn against it by the cleats. The roadway is left flat where it meets it.

components.name: Bolt cleat, port, No. 1
components.what: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 0.7 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

components.name: Bolt cleat, port, No. 2
components.what: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 1.5 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

components.name: Bolt cleat, port, No. 3
components.what: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 3.3 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

components.name: Bolt cleat, port, No. 4
components.what: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 4.4 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

components.name: Bolt cleat, starboard, No. 1
components.what: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 0.7 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

components.name: Bolt cleat, starboard, No. 2
components.what: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 1.5 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

components.name: Bolt cleat, starboard, No. 3
components.what: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 3.3 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

components.name: Bolt cleat, starboard, No. 4
components.what: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 4.4 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

components.name: Hook cleat, port
components.what: At the door's head: an arm on a pivot under a hanger, with a tooth that stands up abaft a pin on the ramp. To let go, its cylinder drops the arm 35 degrees. A switch on it says when it is home.

components.name: Hook cleat, starboard
components.what: At the door's head: an arm on a pivot under a hanger, with a tooth that stands up abaft a pin on the ramp. To let go, its cylinder drops the arm 35 degrees. A switch on it says when it is home.

components.name: Ramp control stand
components.what: A steel desk on the main deck beside the door, port side, against the mooring station's wall: whoever works it stands inboard of it with the ramp's foot at the left hand. On the desk: the emergency stop, a start and a stop button for each main pump, and two spring-centred levers, CLEATS (lock, open) and RAMP (raise, lower). On the upstand: two pressure indicators, 0 to 250 bar (SYSTEM: the pumps' pressure; RAMP LINE A: what carries the leaf, 189 bar with it level), eight lamp windows (power on, pump 1 running, pump 2 running, ramp closed, cleats locked, cleats open, oil level, oil temperature), the key switch that gives the control to the stand or to the bridge, lamp test, horn, and the instructions engraved. Interlocked: no lever does anything until a pump runs; the ramp is not lowered until the cleats are open; the cleats are not locked until the ramp is home; the emergency stop trips both pumps and holds the ramp. A beacon on its top is lit while the ramp is neither locked nor landed. Its door opens on the terminals of X1.

components.name: Junction box of the ramp's switches
components.what: On the port mooring station's wall behind the control stand: the ten cleats' switches, the two latches' and the two door switches are joined here to the stand, to the bridge's door and ramp panel and to the alarm system.

components.name: Door switch, port
components.what: On the door post: closed by the raised ramp when it is home against its seal. With the ten cleats' and the two latches' switches it makes "ramp closed and locked".

components.name: Door switch, starboard
components.what: On the door post: closed by the raised ramp when it is home against its seal. With the ten cleats' and the two latches' switches it makes "ramp closed and locked".

components.name: Safety latch, port
components.what: On the door post at breast height. It needs no oil to hold: an arm on a pivot whose tooth falls by its own weight behind a striker pin on the ramp as the ramp comes home, and stays there. It is lifted 30 degrees to let the ramp go, by a small cylinder on the cleats' let-go line or, with no oil, by pressing down its handle; a pin through arm and bracket secures it for the sea passage. It lets go first and falls in last. A switch on it says when it is home.

components.name: Safety latch, starboard
components.what: On the door post at breast height. It needs no oil to hold: an arm on a pivot whose tooth falls by its own weight behind a striker pin on the ramp as the ramp comes home, and stays there. It is lifted 30 degrees to let the ramp go, by a small cylinder on the cleats' let-go line or, with no oil, by pressing down its handle; a pin through arm and bracket secures it for the sea passage. It lets go first and falls in last. A switch on it says when it is home.

components.name: Stern ramp power pack (HPU-R)
components.what: A tank of about 1,500 litres on a drip tray, with the two main pumps and the cleats' pump on its lid, a level glass, a breather and filler, level and temperature switches. It works the stern ramp and its cleats; the ramp cover over the fixed ramp is to be worked from it too.

components.name: Main pump No. 1
components.what: A pump of 100 l/min at 210 bar under a 37 kW motor on the tank's lid. One pump works the ramp at half speed.

components.name: Main pump No. 2
components.what: As No. 1. With both running the ramp is raised from its lowest in about a minute and a half.

components.name: Cleat pump
components.what: A small pump under a 4 kW motor: it works the ten cleats, so that they can be locked and let go with the main pumps stopped.

components.name: Oil cooler
components.what: An air-blast cooler in the return line, on the tank's after end, with a 1.1 kW fan.

components.name: Pressure block
components.what: On the tank's lid: a non-return valve after each pump, the pressure filter, the relief valve set to 210 bar and the pressure gauge.

components.name: Return filter
components.what: In the return to the tank, with a clogging indicator.

components.name: Hand pump
components.what: On the tank's inboard side: with no power the cleats and, slowly, the ramp are worked by it through the same valves.

components.name: Valve stand
components.what: On the inboard wall: three lever valves with solenoids (the ramp, the cleats, and one for the ramp cover), each worked from the control stand or here by hand; a gauge for each of the ramp's two lines, and two pressure transmitters (PT1 the system, PT2 line A) for the control stand's indicators. The cleats must be free before the ramp's valve can lower it.

components.name: Stern ramp starter panel (RSP)
components.what: On the hydraulic pump room's forward wall. Its door opens on the isolator, the two star-delta starters, the two direct starters, the control transformer and the terminals.
